To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a longitudinal, base-toapex perfusion gradient was present in patients with coronary disease and in patients with coronary risks factors but not in young normal subjects.
a longitudinal, base-toapex myocardial perfusions gradient exists in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) risk factors and is attributed to diffuse coronary artery luminal narrowing.
an abnormal longitudinal, base to apex myocardial perfusion gradients is observed during hyperemia in a cohort of subjects with coronary risk factors without coronary disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of coronary risk factors (CRF) on myocardial perfusion.
the development and evaluation of new techniques for the non-invasive measurement of myocardial blood flow.
the development of a novel approach to the study of the coronary artery disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the abnormal longitudinal, base to apex perfusion gradient observed in the “at risk” group is suggestive of the presence of a coronary flow reserve abnormality associated with coronary risk factor, possibly reflecting developing atherosclerosis and/or preclinical CAD.

the longitudinal, base-to- apex perfusion gradient in coronary artery disease is a result of the diffuse nature of coronary atherosclerotic disease and not a result of the presence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
an abnormal longitudinal, base to apex perfusion gradient observed in patients with coronary disease was also present in patients with coronary risks factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the abnormal longitudinal, base to apex myocardial perfusion observed in patients with coronary disease is also observed in patients with risk factors for coronary artery disease.
a normal myocardial perfusion study in patients with coronary disease risk factors does not exclude the presence of coronary disease.

the abnormal longitudinal, base to apex perfusion gradient observed by PET in patients with coronary disease is also present in patients with coronary heart disease risk factors but without coronary disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a longitudinal, base-to apex perfusion gradient exists in the normal heart and that this gradient increases in patients with risk factors.
we have demonstrated that a longitudinal, base-to apex myocardial perfusion gradients exist in the absence of coronary artery disease.
a normal myocardial perfusion scan does not exclude the presence of an abnormal myocardial blood flow, which is not detected by qualitative analysis.
